root_cause.text: `f2fs_fill_super()` failed to normalize the positive return value from `f2fs_recover_fsync_data()` during read-only `norecovery`/`disable_roll_forward` mounts, so a non-fatal recovery status was propagated as an error to VFS instead of being cleared for readonly mounts.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0)` to explicitly handle `err > 0` in both cases, setting `-EINVAL` only for read-write mounts and `err = 0` with `f2fs_info(sbi, "drop all fsynced data")` for read-only mounts; the CVE description says the bug was “returning a positive error number to vfs_get_tree()”, triggering “get_tree() didn't set fc->root, returned 1” and a kernel BUG.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow read-only F2FS mounts to proceed by dropping unrecoverable fsynced data while preserving the existing error path for writable mounts.
intent_record.what: In `f2fs_fill_super()`, the post-`f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, true)` handling was changed from rejecting only the case `!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0` to first checking `err > 0`, then: if the filesystem is not read-only, logging an error and returning `-EINVAL` via `goto free_meta`; otherwise, logging an informational message `drop all fsynced data` and forcing `err = 0`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, recovery now distinguishes between read-write and read-only mounts when fsync-recovery reports pending data. A writable mount still fails if fsynced data must be recovered, but a read-only mount no longer errors out; instead it explicitly allows mounting by discarding that fsynced data and continuing with success.

grouping_result.intent: Allow read-only F2FS mounts to proceed by dropping unrecoverable fsynced data while preserving the existing error path for writable mounts.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes read-only F2FS mount handling so a positive recovery status from fsync recovery is not treated as a fatal error on readonly/norecovery mounts, while keeping the error path for writable mounts.

candidates.rationale: This call returns a positive non-fatal recovery status, but the pre-fix code did not normalize it for read-only norecovery/disable_roll_forward mounts. As a result, the positive value could be propagated upward as an error instead of being cleared for readonly mounts.

This condition only handles positive recovery results on writable mounts. Before the fix, read-only mounts were not exempted, so the non-fatal positive return from recovery was not normalized properly for readonly mode.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only normalizes positive recovery results for writable mounts. On read-only norecovery/disable_roll_forward mounts, a positive non-fatal return from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() was left unhandled and could be propagated as an error to VFS.

This call can return a positive recovery status that is not necessarily fatal. In the pre-fix code, that return value was not properly normalized for read-only mounts, allowing a non-fatal status to be treated as mount failure.

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/super.c b/fs/f2fs/super.c

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code already contains the normalization/fix logic around `recover_fsync_data()`. In the non-readonly path it calls `err = recover_fsync_data(sbi, false);` and only treats `err < 0` as fatal: `if (err < 0) { ... goto free_kobj; }`, which avoids propagating a positive recovery status as an error. In the readonly branch it explicitly allows a positive return from `recover_fsync_data(sbi, true)` unless the mount is writable: `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0) { err = -EINVAL; ... goto free_kobj; }`. This means the vulnerable construct described in the root cause—failing to normalize a positive recovery return during read-only `norecovery/disable_roll_forward` mounts—is not present here; the code already handles the return value correctly.
